calls.reasoning: Window is 10 NYSE sessions with no earnings for either name (NVDA reported Aug 26, MSFT Jul 29-30; next prints late Oct/Nov), no FOMC, no GTC, no index effective date -- so the largest idiosyncratic jump sources are absent and the reference class is the clean 10-day spread, whose median sits at roughly zero. Median set at +0.3pp: NVDA's beta 2.22 vs MSFT's 1.11 earns a few tenths on normal market drift, offset by short-horizon reversal after NVDA's +5.4% four-session run into Sep 18, quarter-end rotation out of period winners, and a post-hike tape with the 10y near 5% that penalizes the higher-multiple name. Dispersion, not direction, is the forecast: the pair has been trading as a rotation pair (realized correlation ~0 to -0.27) rather than a common-beta pair, which widens the spread materially versus its usual 0.5-0.6 correlation; I assume partial reversion, hence a 5.5pp SD rather than the 8.5pp zero-correlation implication or the 4.9pp small-sample realization. Micron's Sep 30 after-close AI-memory print and the Oct 2 payrolls report fatten both tails without setting direction. No prediction market anywhere prices this relative-return spread, so there is no crowd anchor. Escape mass 2.5% each side: past +15pp needs an NVDA-specific China-access or mega-contract headline against a flat MSFT (NVDA printed +8.74% in one session this sample); past -15pp needs an AI-hardware unwind or export-control shock with MSFT cushioned by software mix.
calls.reconciliation: Four independent runs agreed on the facts that matter and differed mainly on dispersion (12.3 to 15.8pp width) and trivially on center (+0.3 to +0.5). FACTUAL disputes settled from the dossiers: (1) all four confirm no earnings for either name in-window, no FOMC, no GTC (Berlin Oct 20-22, DC Nov 30-Dec 3), no index effective date -- the Sep 18 triple-witching fell before the window; (2) all four independently searched Polymarket, Kalshi and Manifold and found NO contract on NVDA-vs-MSFT relative return, the harness-surfaced Manifold candidate failing on comparator, metric and horizon, so no market anchor exists and none was used; (3) component vol estimates differed (NVDA 29-42% annualized) but the spread is explained by which earnings-reaction days each run included -- Run 3's 42% retains NVDA's Aug 27/28 pair, Runs 2/4's ~29% excludes it, and the ex-earnings figure is the right conditioning for this window. UNSETTLED factual dispute: NVDA's year-to-date return, quoted at ~+4-5% by Run 1 and ~+30% by Runs 2/4 (Run 2's +30.5% is explicitly trailing-12-month, which can coexist with a lower YTD only if the 52-week low near $164 printed around the turn of the year). No web access this run to break it; its bearing is small since cross-sectional momentum operates at multi-month, not two-week, horizons, so I held the median near zero rather than picking a side. Also unsettled: Run 3's Oct 1 federal funding cliff vs Run 4's specific claim that a Sep 2 continuing resolution funds through Dec 11 -- Run 4's is the more precisely dated claim and I lean to it, but the residual risk is common-factor and largely cancels in a spread. JUDGMENT calls I took rather than split: the sub-iid realized 10-day dispersion is real but rests on ~5 independent windows in a calm range-bound sample, so I weighted it against implied vols rather than adopting it, landing at 14.0pp width -- inside the runs' range but arrived at from the vol/correlation decomposition, not from averaging them; and I assume the anomalous ~0 pair correlation partially reverts toward its AI-cycle norm, which is the single largest lever on this number and the thing I would most want to observe in the window's first sessions.
